goal: Implement chosen Compact №3 design across Workspace renderer with a single upper toolbar, preserve all existing actions/data, verify the 56-case edge matrix at 1440x960 and 1024x720, and deliver reviewed local commit and evidence.
hypothesis: Scoped semantic palette and layout changes in existing renderer components can produce the compact design while retaining current handlers, service contracts, tab lifecycle, persistence, keyboard access and project data.
scope: Renderer UI components/styles and corresponding UI documentation and focused tests; isolated temporary fixtures only. No storage, IPC, Electron security, project identity/status rules, backend or live user files.
constraints: No invented actions from illustrations; no push/merge/release. Independent verifier checks frozen attempt before completion. Explicit unverified reason and next step for any matrix row not executable.

checks.description: Relevant Node tests, npm run typecheck, npm run build:renderer and git diff --check pass on changed version; failure of any command falsifies.

Existing source-backed actions, tab lifecycle, property editors/settings and renderer-only boundary remain reachable without changed storage/IPC/security/project IDs/status; any lost handler, data regression or invented action falsifies.

At 1440x960 and 1024x720 UI uses one upper row with textual horizontally scrollable view/project tabs and pinned actions; Add View/Customize icons lack labels/hover backdrop while retaining tooltip, accessible names and visible focus; any clipped required action, second toolbar row or inaccessible tab falsifies.

All 56 matrix IDs have actual result or specific unverified reason and next step, covering long names/overflow, empty/error, editors, keyboard and measured contrast; missing row or unsupported pass claim falsifies.

Changed UI and docs are reviewable via local commit and report with screenshot paths, checks, limitations and commit hash; unavailable artifact, uncommitted intended change or missing review evidence falsifies.
